Alarms.Alarm Summary: No issue—pings from server and remote-worker successful (0% loss, low latency).
Alarms.Recommended Actions:
- No immediate remediation required; connectivity is healthy (0% packet loss, low RTT).
- Continue monitoring; set alerts for packet loss >1% or RTT >10 ms.
- From the Cisco gateway, verify with:
  - ping 10.1.0.2 repeat 50 timeout 2
  - ping 10.0.1.2 repeat 50 timeout 2
  - show ip interface brief
  - show interfaces | include errors|drops
  - show ip route 10.1.0.2
  - show ip route 10.0.1.2
- If an alert was raised despite healthy pings, adjust/suppress the alarm thresholds and document the baseline latency.
Alarms.Tracking Next Steps:
- Continue monitoring with scheduled pings from both the server and remote-worker for the next 24–48 hours (1–5 minute intervals). Current baseline: 0% loss, ~2 ms RTT.
- Trigger alerts if any packet loss is sustained for ≥5 minutes or if latency increases >3x baseline for ≥5 minutes.
- On any alert, immediately collect MTR/traceroute from both ends, interface counters (errors/drops), link utilization, and relevant firewall/routing logs; compare against baseline.
- If degradation persists >30 minutes or recurs ≥2 times in 24 hours, open a Network Engineering ticket with timestamps, ping/MTR outputs, and interface stats; escalate to the ISP if MTR indicates upstream hop loss.
